title: Comparing Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Kindergarten Comparing length, mass and capacity Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Direct comparative measurement (e.g., linear, mass, capacity): using a baseline for direct comparison in linear measurement; height, width, length; heavier than, lighter than, same as; holds more, holds less
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on comparing length, mass and capacity for the BC curriculum: longer and shorter, taller, heavier and lighter on a balance, holds more and less, and using a baseline. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Line things up at one end before you compare length.
key_sub: The heavier side of a balance goes down. Pour to see which container holds more.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Length: line things up at one end (a baseline), then see which goes further: longer, shorter, taller, wider.
  • Mass: on a pan balance, the heavier side goes down. A big thing is not always heavier.
  • Capacity: pour from one container into another to see which holds more.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Comparing without a baselineLine up one end first, then compare the other end.
Thinking bigger means heavierUse a balance. A big beach ball is lighter than a small rock.
Thinking taller always holds morePour water from one into the other to check.

faq.q: What is direct comparison in measurement?
faq.a: Comparing two things by putting them next to each other, without numbers: longer or shorter, heavier or lighter, holds more or holds less.
Lining things up at one end makes the comparison fair. Otherwise a shorter thing can look longer.
By holding one in each hand or using a pan balance. The heavier side goes down.
By filling one container and pouring into another. If it overflows, the first holds more.
